response.message:
I've drafted the full IBM Cloud flow on the board: consent gate, audio ingestion, Watson Speech to Text, PII redaction, grounded suggestions from watsonx.ai and watsonx Discovery, a summary the agent approves, and a CRM update left as a draft for the agent to submit. Nothing places calls or writes to the CRM automatically. Regions stay "To be selected", and nothing has been deployed or checked for account access. For the first local test, we'd play a synthetic recorded call through fixtures to check the flow: no recording before consent, redaction before the model, citations attached and the CRM left untouched. The model's replies in that test are scripted, so they can't tell us how good the suggestions are. That needs a separate check against a real watsonx.ai model in an approved account, using labelled synthetic calls.

If the caller says no to recording, should the agent still get live suggestions without saving any audio, or should the assistant switch off for that call?

proposal.title: IBM Cloud agent-assist for synthetic support calls (first end-to-end sketch)
proposal.body: Scope: consent capture, audio ingestion, Watson Speech to Text transcription, PII redaction before any model call, grounded suggestions (watsonx.ai + watsonx Discovery over existing KB), agent-approved call summary and a CRM draft the agent submits manually. Assumptions: synthetic data only; existing telephony, KB and CRM are outside provisioning scope; regions, plans, model access and account entitlements unverified; no outbound calls or automatic CRM writes. Only design intent; no native IBM generator exists for these components yet, so engineering is required.

response.message:
Here's what the local check shows: it found no failed tests, and the full end-to-end design is still intact. The "blocked" status means there's nothing to run yet, not that the design is wrong. The first finding is the synthetic caller and existing telephony. Both are correctly marked as existing outside systems, so they need a reference plan, not a fix to the diagram. The real blocker is that the IBM blocks (consent gate, ingestion, Object Storage, Speech to Text, redaction and the orchestrator) don't have a supported implementation yet. Today's typed contracts only cover narrow cases, like IBM Object Storage on its own, and none of them do this job. That's product engineering work, and changing the diagram won't fix it. The reproducer is this artifact (ecc25d7f…, revision 2): we need typed IBM implementations, starting with a Code Engine consent gate that fails closed and is backed by PostgreSQL. I won't swap in a narrower contract, because that would shrink the scope. No model, region or account access has been checked.

So that the implementation brief is precise, here's the next question: how does your telephony hand over consent and audio? For example, a SIP media fork, a WebSocket stream or a recording webhook. Both the consent gate and ingestion depend on that contract.
